name: Shoals Technologies Group, Inc.
reason: Solar EBOS supplier tied to utility-scale solar build cycles and policy (IRA credits), with EBIT margin falling from 21.2% to 11.9%, adjusted EPS 0.55x 10y peak, wire-shrinkback warranty/litigation overhang and a large adjusted-vs-GAAP gap (258%); no durable moat to forecast.

name: Trinity Capital, Inc.
reason: Externally-levered venture-debt BDC (net debt/EBITDA 5.9x) whose earnings are set by credit cycles and rates; NII per share flat ~2.1 since 2022 and consensus shows 0% FY1 and -6.9% FY3 growth.

name: Dime Commercial Bancshares, Inc.
reason: NY commercial bank with heavy multifamily/CRE exposure and rate-sensitive margin; adjusted EPS 2.59 in 2025 vs 3.77 in 2022 (0.69x peak, 5y CAGR 0.5%) with share count up 11.5%/yr from the Bridge merger, so no evidence of a low-cost-deposit compounder.

name: Expand Energy Corporation
reason: Natural gas E&P (Chesapeake/Southwestern merger) whose earnings are set by Henry Hub prices; EPS history swings from large losses to profits and shares up 53.5%/yr from restructuring/merger.

name: Sprinklr, Inc.
reason: Customer-experience SaaS with slowing growth, only 6.9% EBIT margin after years of losses (10y ROIC -7.3%), GAAP EPS 0.09 in 2025 and consensus FY1 -2.5%; crowded market and AI disintermediation risk, no specialness.

name: Oscar Health, Inc.
reason: ACA-exchange health insurer dependent on government subsidies and risk adjustment; GAAP losses in 6 of 7 years (2025 EPS -1.69) and 10y ROIC -40.9% make earnings unforecastable.

name: Coursera Inc
reason: Online-learning platform with GAAP losses every year (EBIT margin -8.3% at best), facing direct AI disintermediation of courseware and slowing consumer demand; nothing durable to forecast.

name: Applovin Corp.
reason: Exceptional economics (EBIT margin 76.4%, EPS 10.04 in 2025 from 0.98 in 2023) but EPS and margin are at 1.0x/100th pctile of a short history, results hinge on an opaque ad-ranking model plus Apple/Google platform rules, and the e-commerce expansion is unproven; cannot forecast 10 years with confidence.

name: Sable Offshore Corp.
reason: Single-asset offshore California oil restart with binary regulatory/litigation outcomes, no profitable history (2025 EPS -4.18) and oil-price-driven earnings.

name: Pagaya Technologies Ltd
reason: AI underwriting network whose fee income depends on ABS funding markets and consumer credit cycles; GAAP losses 2021-2024, first profit in 2025 (EBIT margin 19.2% at a high), 10y ROIC -32%.

name: GXO Logistics, Inc.
reason: Contract logistics with thin 3.2% EBIT margin, 10y ROIC 2.0%, acquisitions at 1.85x cumulative FCF (Wincanton, PFSweb) and net debt/EBITDA 5.7x; GAAP EPS 0.28 in 2025 is 0.14x peak.

name: Gulfport Energy Corp
reason: Natural gas E&P with earnings set by commodity prices; emerged from 2021 bankruptcy and EPS swung from 66.33 in 2023 to -14.72 in 2024.

name: N-able, Inc.
reason: MSP-focused RMM/security software with slowing growth, EBIT margin down to 10.8% from 19.6%, GAAP loss in 2025, net debt/EBITDA 3.2x and acquisitions (Adlumin); ordinary business in a competitive niche.

name: TaskUs, Inc.
reason: Outsourced content-moderation/CX provider with heavy single-customer concentration (Meta) and direct AI-automation threat to its labor model; EPS 1.0x peak with margin at 100th pctile and consensus FY1 -18.6%.

name: Core & Main, Inc.
reason: Leading water/wastewater distributor with secular infrastructure tailwinds, but EPS stepped from 0.68 to 2.13 in 2022 on PVC pipe price inflation and has been flat since (2.31 in 2025, 1.0x 10y max), with growth reliant on roll-up M&A (acq 0.59x FCF) and construction-cycle exposure; underlying organic earnings power is hard to pin down.

name: First Advantage Corp.
reason: Background-screening provider tied to hiring volumes, levered at 4.7x net debt/EBITDA after the Sterling acquisition (acq 2.58x cumulative FCF), with GAAP losses in 2024-2025 and 10y ROIC -1.1%.

name: nCino, Inc.
reason: Sticky bank loan-origination software, but GAAP EBIT margin only 3.5% after years of losses, acquisitions 6.6x cumulative FCF, a very large adjusted-vs-GAAP gap, and dependence on bank tech budgets and the Salesforce platform make long-run earnings hard to forecast.

name: Kyndryl Holdings, Inc.
reason: IBM spin-off in legacy IT infrastructure outsourcing with declining revenue, 4.2% EBIT margin, 10y ROIC -14.7% and GAAP EPS falling 19.6% in 2025; a turnaround story with no durable moat.

name: GE Healthcare Technologies, Inc.
reason: Global imaging oligopoly (with Siemens/Philips) plus recurring service and pharmaceutical diagnostics, stable EBIT margin 14-16% for 6 years, net debt/EBITDA 1.7x, 10y ROIC 11.6% and consensus EPS growth 10-11% for FY2-FY3; watch China procurement and tariffs, and GAAP EPS 5y CAGR is only 0.6% due to the 2023 spin-off.

name: Crescent Energy Co.
reason: Oil and gas producer whose earnings are set by commodity prices and whose growth is acquisition-driven (acq 1.17x cumulative FCF) with net debt/EBITDA 2.9x; 2025 EPS 0.54 is 0.25x peak.
